name: Hosea the prophet
charge: Taking a wife of whoredoms at the Lord’s command as a sign against Israel; prophesying the scattering and the return
summary: In the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, the Lord told Hosea to take a wife of whoredoms, because the land had left the Lord for other lovers, and he took Gomer and named her children Jezreel, Lo-ruhamah and Lo-ammi as the sentence on the northern kingdom (Hosea 1:1-9). Told again to love an adulteress, he bought her back and kept her many days, a sign that Israel would live many days without king or sacrifice and afterward return to the Lord and David their king (Hosea 3:1-5). The same prophet carried the promise that the children of Israel would be as the sand of the sea and be called sons of the living God (Hosea 1:10-11).
offenseFull: The word of the Lord came to Hosea the son of Beeri in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz and Hezekiah kings of Judah, and of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel (Hosea 1:1); he and Isaiah shared the same four kings of Judah. The Lord told him to go and take a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms, because the land had left the Lord for other lovers, and he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim (Hosea 1:2-3). He took a whore because it was a picture of how the people committed spiritual fornication against the Most High, devising idols and keeping the customs of other nations (Wisdom of Solomon 14:12). God was showing Hosea that he would go through what God goes through, with Israel as the bride.

The Lord named the children. The first son was Jezreel, for in a little while He would punish the house of Jehu for the blood of Jezreel and end the kingdom of the house of Israel, breaking Israel’s bow in the valley of Jezreel (Hosea 1:4-5). The daughter was Lo-ruhamah, for He would no longer have mercy on the house of Israel, though He would have mercy on Judah and save them by the Lord their God, not by bow or sword (Hosea 1:6-7). The second son was Lo-ammi, for they were not His people and He would not be their God (Hosea 1:8-9). The names say cut off three times, and they were fulfilled when Assyria carried Israel away (2 Kings 17:6). When a people are no longer God’s people they become strangers, heathen, Gentiles; the Gentiles all through Paul’s letters are this chapter.

Then the Lord told him to go again and love a woman loved by another, an adulteress, as the Lord loves the children of Israel though they turn to other gods; he bought her for fifteen pieces of silver and a measure and a half of barley, and told her she would stay with him many days and not play the harlot or belong to another man (Hosea 3:1-3). By the law a man could not take back a wife who had gone to another, yet the Lord lets Israel return (Jeremiah 3:1). The captivity itself is mercy compared with being cut off altogether.
judgmentFull: Yet the number of the children of Israel would be as the sand of the sea, beyond measuring or counting, and where it was said to them that they were not His people, it would be said that they were sons of the living God (Hosea 1:10). Paul reads it of the called (Romans 9:24-26): Ephraim was cast down but not cast away. The study notes teach that the sand of the sea is the blacks, Hispanics and Native Americans, not the so-called white man calling himself a Jew, and that the multitude is one sign of who the people of God are. Then Judah and Israel would be gathered together, appoint themselves one head, and come up out of the land, for great would be the day of Jezreel (Hosea 1:11): the northern and southern kingdoms coming together under God’s laws with one head, Christ, needing no other nation to put its stamp on it.

The children of Israel would live many days without a king, without a prince, without a sacrifice, without an image, without an ephod and without household gods (Hosea 3:4). Without a king is political sovereignty, lost when Europe colonized Africa and the slave ships took us. Without a sacrifice is no religious establishment teaching us our God; the slave

master taught us his. Without an image, our image was destroyed, and worshipping a god who does not look like you destroys the way you see yourself. Without an ephod is no priest to guide. The classes set the many days beside the time, times and a half of Daniel, reckoned as three hundred and fifty years, until the power of the holy people is scattered (Daniel 12:7); other teaching speaks of the many days as centuries. Afterward the children of Israel would return and seek the Lord their God and David their king, and come trembling to the Lord and His goodness in the last days (Hosea 3:5). David their king is Christ, the king the Lord said He would raise up to them when He breaks the yoke from their neck and saves them from the land of their captivity (Jeremiah 30:8-10). The afterward is today: we are returning.

text.text: The word of the Lord that came unto Hosea, the son of Beeri, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel.

The beginning of the word of the Lord by Hosea. And the Lord said to Hosea, Go, take unto thee a wife of whoredoms and children of whoredoms: for the land hath committed great whoredom, departing from the Lord.
So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim; which conceived, and bare him a son.
And the Lord said unto him, Call his name Jezreel; for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu, and will cause to cease the kingdom of the house of Israel.
And it shall come to pass at that day, that I will break the bow of Israel in the valley of Jezreel.
And she conceived again, and bare a daughter. And God said unto him, Call her name Lo–ruhamah: for I will no more have mercy upon the house of Israel; but I will utterly take them away.
But I will have mercy upon the house of Judah, and will save them by the Lord their God, and will not save them by bow, nor by sword, nor by battle, by horses, nor by horsemen.
Now when she had weaned Lo–ruhamah, she conceived, and bare a son.
Then said God, Call his name Lo–ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.

Then said the Lord unto me, Go yet, love a woman beloved of her friend, yet an adulteress, according to the love of the Lord toward the children of Israel, who look to other gods, and love flagons of wine.
So I bought her to me for fifteen pieces of silver, and for an homer of barley, and an half homer of barley:
And I said unto her, Thou shalt abide for me many days; thou shalt not play the harlot, and thou shalt not be for another man: so will I also be for thee.
For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim:
Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.

Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.
Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel.

They say, If a man put away his wife, and she go from him, and become another man’s, shall he return unto her again? shall not that land be greatly polluted? but thou hast played the harlot with many lovers; yet return again to me, saith the Lord.

Yet the number of the children of Israel shall be as the sand of the sea, which cannot be measured nor numbered; and it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people, there it shall be said unto them, Ye are the sons of the living God.
Even us, whom he hath called, not of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles?
As he saith also in Osee, I will call them my people, which were not my people; and her beloved, which was not beloved.
And it shall come to pass, that in the place where it was said unto them, Ye are not my people; there shall they be called the children of the living God.
Then shall the children of Judah and the children of Israel be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel.
For the children of Israel shall abide many days without a king, and without a prince, and without a sacrifice, and without an image, and without an ephod, and without teraphim:

And I heard the man clothed in linen, which was upon the waters of the river, when he held up his right hand and his left hand unto heaven, and sware by him that liveth for ever that it shall be for a time, times, and an half; and when he shall have accomplished to scatter the power of the holy people, all these things shall be finished.
Afterward shall the children of Israel return, and seek the Lord their God, and David their king; and shall fear the Lord and his goodness in the latter days.
For it shall come to pass in that day, saith the Lord of hosts, that I will break his yoke from off thy neck, and will burst thy bonds, and strangers shall no more serve themselves of him:
But they shall serve the Lord their God, and David their king, whom I will raise up unto them.

Therefore fear thou not, O my servant Jacob, saith the Lord; neither be dismayed, O Israel: for, lo, I will save thee from afar, and thy seed from the land of their captivity; and Jacob shall return, and shall be in rest, and be quiet, and none shall make him afraid.
